items.title: Senior AI Agent & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer Needed to Productionize Autonomous Browser Platform
items.description:
Orbit AI Technologies Corporation is building Orbit, a consumer AI agent designed to complete real-world tasks on a user's behalf. Rather than simply answering questions, Orbit is designed to research, navigate websites, use applications, complete multi-step workflows, request approval when necessary, and verify that a task was completed successfully.

We already have an existing application, Browser Engine, and Google Cloud deployment. This is not a greenfield project. We need an experienced engineer to evaluate what we've built and turn the existing system into reliable production infrastructure.

What you'll work on the project includes:
- Persistent, isolated cloud computers for AI agents
- Chromium/Playwright browser automation
- Website navigation, form completion, clicking, and information extraction
- Persistent authenticated browser sessions
- Long-running and asynchronous Mission execution
- Mission state persistence and recovery after interruptions
- Multiple concurrent agents/workers
- User takeover of an agent's browser
- Sign-in, 2FA, CAPTCHA, and other human-handoff workflows
- Approval checkpoints before consequential actions
- Secure file creation/read/write capabilities
- Controlled shell/tool execution
- Redis/PostgreSQL-backed state
- APIs and real-time communication between the frontend and Browser Engine
- Logging, monitoring, retries, queues, and failure recovery
- Secrets management and credential security
- User/environment isolation
- Deployment, scaling, backups, and infrastructure hardening on Google Cloud
Longer term, we also want Orbit to support authorized execution on users' computers and mobile devices.

Existing technology
Our current environment includes Google Cloud Platform, Linux, Node.js/TypeScript, Chromium/Playwright, PM2/Nginx, and browser automation infrastructure.
We're open to architectural changes when there is a clear technical reason for them. We specifically want someone capable of advising us on what should be kept, replaced, or redesigned.

Who we're looking for
You should have strong production experience with:
Google Cloud Platform, Playwright/Chromium, Node.js/TypeScript and/or Python, Docker, Linux, backend APIs, Redis/PostgreSQL, asynchronous/background jobs, security, monitoring, and production deployments.
Experience building AI agents, computer-use systems, persistent browser environments, browser streaming/takeover, multi-tenant infrastructure, or human-in-the-loop autonomous systems is highly desirable.

We're not looking primarily for prompt engineering or a basic chatbot developer. This role requires substantial backend, cloud, browser-automation, and systems engineering experience.

Initial deliverables
The engagement will begin with:
1. Audit the existing Orbit architecture and Google Cloud deployment.
2. Document security, reliability, scalability, and architectural issues.
3. Establish a proper development/staging environment.
4. Productionize persistent Mission and browser execution.
5. Implement reliable state persistence, recovery, and concurrent execution.
6. Implement secure user takeover and authentication handoffs.
7. Implement approvals, audit logging, monitoring, and emergency-stop controls.
8. Demonstrate a reliable end-to-end Mission through the Orbit interface.
9. Document the resulting infrastructure so Orbit isn't dependent on one contractor to operate it.

Engagement
This is initially a 3–6 month contract. You'll work largely independently and directly with Orbit's leadership. We're specifically looking for someone who can provide technical guidance, not simply implement tickets.
Please include examples of production systems you've personally built involving browser automation, cloud infrastructure, AI agents, long-running jobs, or similar autonomous systems. Briefly explain your role and the architecture involved.

Please do not submit a generic AI-generated proposal. (AI will be detected and declined automatically) We're primarily interested in your relevant engineering experience and examples of systems you've actually shipped.

7. Implement approvals, audit logging, monitoring, and emergency-stop controls.
8. Demonstrate a reliable end-to-end Mission through the Orbit interface.
9. Document the resulting infrastructure so Orbit isn't dependent on one contractor to operate it.

Engagement
This is initially a 3–6 month contract. You'll work largely independently and directly with Orbit's leadership. We're specifically looking for someone who can provide technical guidance, not simply implement tickets.
Please include examples of production systems you've personally built involving browser automation, cloud infrastructure, AI agents, long-running jobs, or similar autonomous systems. Briefly explain your role and the architecture involved.

Please do not submit a generic AI-generated proposal. (AI will be detected and declined automatically) We're primarily interested in your relevant engineering experience and examples of systems you've actually shipped.

items.title: Python developer to stabilize an AI content generation pipeline (APIs, ffmpeg, Linux)
items.description:
I run an automated content production pipeline in production on a Linux server (Python, systemd). It receives customer orders, generates images, video clips and audio through several third-party AI APIs (image, video, voice, LLM), runs automated quality checks, edits the final video with ffmpeg and delivers it to the customer.

It works, but it is not reliable:
- too many wasted regenerations, so costs per order run over budget
- quality checks reject good outputs and miss bad ones
- the job queue gets stuck and deliveries are late
- code is changed directly in production, with no test environment

What I need:
1. Guardrails in code: max retries per step, spend cap per order, never delete generated files, never re-run finished steps
2. Unblock and speed up the queue (parallel jobs, faster ffmpeg encoding)
3. Simplify the automated quality checks
4. A test environment (run on a copy of an order, dry-run mode with no paid API calls) and a safe deployment process
5. A simple status report: pending / in progress / delivered / average cost / alerts

Stack: Python 3, systemd, ffmpeg, REST APIs, Git. Nice to have: Cloudflare Workers, Shopify, Telegram bots.

Start ASAP. Short mission first, ongoing work possible if it goes well.

To apply, tell me:
- a pipeline or automation you made reliable in production, and how
- how you would add a spend cap and a retry limit to a multi-step job pipeline

items.title: Seasonal Customer Support Associate
items.description:
Role Overview

The Client Support Associate plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional end-to-end customer experience. You will manage customer inquiries, ensure timely responses aligned with service-level targets, and take full ownership of issue resolution.

This is a contract role with a potential to turn into a full time permanent position. This role goes beyond traditional support—you are expected to analyze problems, take ownership, and proactively contribute to improvements that enhance customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.

You will collaborate closely with Purchasing, Engineers, Logistics teams, and Partner merchants to ensure seamless order resolution, particularly for complex cases such as returns, delays, and discrepancies.

Key Responsibilities
1. Manage inbound customer inquiries via email and support platforms, ensuring timely, accurate, and  professional responses
2.  Own tickets end-to-end, from first response through resolution
3.  Meet defined SLA targets for response and resolution times
4.  Investigate and resolve issues related to:
* Order delays and cancellations
* Returns and refunds
* Shipping and delivery concerns
* Product discrepancies
5. Coordinate with internal and external teams (Purchasing, Logistics, Engineers, Merchants) to resolve complex cases
6. Maintain clear and consistent communication with customers, setting expectations and providing updates
7. Identify recurring issues and escalate trends to support process improvements
8. Ensure accurate documentation and updates within support systems
9. Support return operations, including tracking timelines and managing expectations
10. Contribute to improving workflows, templates, and support processes

More About You
* 1-3 years of experience in customer support, e-commerce, or operations
* Strong written and verbal communication skills—clear, professional, and empathetic
* Ability to manage high-volume workloads while maintaining accuracy and quality
* Experience with support platforms (e.g., Freshdesk, Zendesk)
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Ability to handle escalations with composure and ownership
* Highly detail-oriented and organized
* Comfortable working in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment
* Familiarity with SLAs, KPIs, and performance tracking
* Strong collaboration skills across cross-functional teams
* Understand return operations and refund workflows

Bonus Points If You…
* Have experience in luxury e-commerce, fashion, or marketplace platforms
* Are hungry for growth and continuously seek to improve
* Are an AI enthusiast and interested in leveraging tools to improve productivity
* Take initiative and proactively identify areas for improvement
* Communicate clearly and thrive in collaborative environments
* Adapt quickly in a rapidly evolving organization

Why Join Us?
* Work with a globally distributed team
* Be part of a fast-growing luxury e-commerce platform
* Opportunity to convert into a full-time permanent position
* Exposure to operations, data, and cross-functional strategy
* A culture that values ownership, initiative, and continuous improvement
* Fully remote role

Meta fields

URL redirects

Internal links

Do not delete, rename, reorganize, or make major changes to products, collections, URLs, or store structure without approval.

Shopify themes

items.title: SharePoint / Power Automate Specialist for Accounting Firm Document Archive
items.description:
# Upwork Project Description — SharePoint / Power Automate Specialist for Accounting Firm Document Archive

## Project Title

**SharePoint & Power Automate Specialist Needed to Build Client Document Archive for CPA Firm**

## Project Description

We are a Canadian CPA accounting firm moving to a fully online operating model. We need a SharePoint / Power Automate specialist to help us implement a structured document archive for our corporate clients.

The professional filing structure has already been designed internally. We are not looking for someone to redesign the accounting workflow. We need a technical specialist to implement the SharePoint structure and automate folder creation using Power Automate.

The archive will be used to organize client documents such as corporate year-end files, financial statements, T2 / CO-17 tax returns, GST/QST filings, payroll records, T4/RL-1 summaries, T5/RL-3 dividend slips, CRA/Revenu Québec correspondence, engagement letters, client communications, and permanent corporate records.

## Scope of Work

The project will include the following:

### 1. Review Existing Structure

Review our proposed SharePoint archive structure and confirm the best technical implementation approach.

The structure will include folders such as:

* Permanent File
* Engagement and Billing
* Fiscal Years
* Payroll - Calendar Years
* T5/RL3 - Calendar Years
* GST/QST General
* CRA/RQ General Correspondence
* Client Communications
* Shareholder and Benefits
* Archive - Superseded

Each client will have its own folder, and each fiscal year will have its own standardized subfolder structure.

### 2. Create or Optimize SharePoint Library

Set up or optimize a SharePoint document library for corporate client files.

The structure should be easy to use by a small accounting team and should support future automation.

### 3. Create Client Master List

Create or assist with creating a SharePoint list to serve as the source for automation.

Expected fields may include:

* Client Legal Name
* Client Short Name
* Business Number
* NEQ
* Fiscal Year-End Date
* GST/QST Filing Frequency
* Payroll Client: Yes/No
* Dividend Client: Yes/No
* T5/RL3 Required: Yes/No
* Client Status
* Responsible Person
* Notes

### 4. Power Automate — New Client Folder Creation

Build a Power Automate flow that creates the main folder structure when a new corporate client is added to the Client Master List.

The flow should create the client folder and all standard top-level subfolders.

### 5. Power Automate — Fiscal Year Folder Creation

Build a flow, either manual or automated, to create a new fiscal year folder for an existing client.

The fiscal year folder should include standardized subfolders for:

* Client Documents Received
* Bookkeeping and Periodic Records
* GST/QST
* Adjusting Entries
* Trial Balance and Working Papers
* Financial Statements
* Compilation Report
* T2 / CO-17 Tax Returns
* T2 Schedules and Tax Working Papers
* T4A
* Dividends and Shareholder Transactions
* Payroll Related to Fiscal Year
* Tax Summaries and Client Letter
* E-Signature and Approvals
* Final Filed Documents
* CRA/RQ Notices Related to Fiscal Year
* Client Communications Related to Fiscal Year
* Other

### 6. GST/QST Period Automation

Create logic to generate GST/QST folders based on the client’s fiscal year-end and GST/QST filing frequency.

The folders should not simply be named Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, because many clients have non-calendar fiscal year-ends.

For example, for a client with a March 31 fiscal year-end and quarterly GST/QST filings, the flow should create folders such as:

* 2025-04-01 to 2025-06-30
* 2025-07-01 to 2025-09-30
* 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31
* 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31

The same logic should support monthly, quarterly, annual, or not applicable GST/QST filing frequencies.

### 7. Payroll and T5/RL3 Calendar Year Folders

Create or assist with flows to generate calendar-year folders for payroll and T5/RL3 documents, where applicable.

Payroll folders may include:

* Payroll Reports
* DAS / PD7A / TPZ Source Deductions
* Payroll Summaries
* T4 Slips and Summary
* RL-1 Slips and Summary
* CNESST / WSIB
* Taxable Benefits
* Car Allowance
* Employee Documents

### 8. Duplicate Prevention and Error Handling

The flows must include reasonable controls to prevent duplicate folder creation.

For example:

* If the client folder already exists, do not recreate it.
* If the fiscal year folder already exists, skip or notify the user.
* If a GST/QST period folder already exists, skip or notify the user.

We would also like a simple automation log or error notification system.

### 9. Permissions and Security Review

Review the proposed access model and recommend a secure but practical permissions structure for a small CPA firm.

We are not necessarily looking for complex folder-level permissions at the beginning, but we want to avoid mistakes that would be difficult to fix later.

### 10. Optional Metadata and Views

If appropriate, recommend and/or configure simple metadata and SharePoint views, such as:

* Client
* Fiscal Year
* Calendar Year
* Document Type
* Status
* Responsible Person

However, the solution should remain practical and easy for the team to use.

## Important Notes

We already have the accounting and professional filing logic. We are looking for technical implementation, automation, and SharePoint best practices.

The ideal solution should be:

* Easy to use by a small accounting team
* Scalable for many corporate clients
* Compatible with clients having different fiscal year-ends
* Compatible with monthly, quarterly, annual, or no GST/QST filing requirements
* Robust enough to avoid duplicate folders and automation errors
* Secure and suitable for confidential client information

## Required Skills

The freelancer should have strong experience with:

* Microsoft SharePoint Online
* Power Automate
* Microsoft 365
* SharePoint document libraries
* SharePoint lists
* Folder automation
* Conditional logic in Power Automate
* Error handling and logging
* Permission management in SharePoint

Experience working with accounting firms, legal firms, professional services firms, or document-heavy environments would be a strong asset.

## Deliverables

Expected deliverables include:

1. Reviewed and confirmed SharePoint implementation plan
2. SharePoint document library structure
3. Client Master List setup or refinement
4. Power Automate flow for new client folder creation
5. Power Automate flow for fiscal year folder creation
6. GST/QST period generation logic
7. Payroll and T5/RL3 calendar year folder logic, if applicable
8. Duplicate prevention logic
9. Basic error logging or notification
10. Short documentation explaining how to use and maintain the flows

## Preferred Approach

We would prefer to start with a short discovery/review session, followed by implementation in stages.

The first stage should be a working prototype using test clients only. Once validated, the automation can be applied to real clients.

## Questions for Applicants

Please answer the following when applying:

1. Have you implemented SharePoint folder automation using Power Automate before?
2. Can you create folders dynamically based on fiscal year-end dates and filing frequencies?
3. How would you prevent duplicate folder creation in Power Automate?
4. Do you recommend using folders only, metadata, document sets, or a hybrid approach for this type of project?
5. Have you worked with professional services firms or confidential client document structures before?
6. Are you able to provide a short handover document at the end of the project?

## Budget

Please provide an estimate based on the scope above. We are open to either a fixed-price project or an hourly arrangement, provided that the work is divided into clear milestones.

The professional filing structure has already been designed internally. We are not looking for someone to redesign the accounting workflow. We need a technical specialist to implement the SharePoint structure and automate folder creation using Power Automate.

The archive will be used to organize client documents such as corporate year-end files, financial statements, T2 / CO-17 tax returns, GST/QST filings, payroll records, T4/RL-1 summaries, T5/RL-3 dividend slips, CRA/Revenu Québec correspondence, engagement letters, client communications, and permanent corporate records.

## Scope of Work

The project will include the following:

### 1. Review Existing Structure

Review our proposed SharePoint archive structure and confirm the best technical implementation approach.

The structure will include folders such as:

* Permanent File
* Engagement and Billing
* Fiscal Years
* Payroll - Calendar Years
* T5/RL3 - Calendar Years
* GST/QST General
* CRA/RQ General Correspondence
* Client Communications
* Shareholder and Benefits
* Archive - Superseded

Each client will have its own folder, and each fiscal year will have its own standardized subfolder structure.

### 2. Create or Optimize SharePoint Library

Set up or optimize a SharePoint document library for corporate client files.

The structure should be easy to use by a small accounting team and should support future automation.

### 3. Create Client Master List

Create or assist with creating a SharePoint list to serve as the source for automation.

Expected fields may include:

* Client Legal Name
* Client Short Name
* Business Number
* NEQ
* Fiscal Year-End Date
* GST/QST Filing Frequency
* Payroll Client: Yes/No
* Dividend Client: Yes/No
* T5/RL3 Required: Yes/No
* Client Status
* Responsible Person
* Notes

### 4. Power Automate — New Client Folder Creation

Build a Power Automate flow that creates the main folder structure when a new corporate client is added to the Client Master List.

The flow should create the client folder and all standard top-level subfolders.

### 5. Power Automate — Fiscal Year Folder Creation

Build a flow, either manual or automated, to create a new fiscal year folder for an existing client.

The fiscal year folder should include standardized subfolders for:

* Client Documents Received
* Bookkeeping and Periodic Records
* GST/QST
* Adjusting Entries
* Trial Balance and Working Papers
* Financial Statements
* Compilation Report
* T2 / CO-17 Tax Returns
* T2 Schedules and Tax Working Papers
* T4A
* Dividends and Shareholder Transactions
* Payroll Related to Fiscal Year
* Tax Summaries and Client Letter
* E-Signature and Approvals
* Final Filed Documents
* CRA/RQ Notices Related to Fiscal Year
* Client Communications Related to Fiscal Year
* Other

### 6. GST/QST Period Automation

Create logic to generate GST/QST folders based on the client’s fiscal year-end and GST/QST filing frequency.

The folders should not simply be named Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, because many clients have non-calendar fiscal year-ends.

For example, for a client with a March 31 fiscal year-end and quarterly GST/QST filings, the flow should create folders such as:

* 2025-04-01 to 2025-06-30
* 2025-07-01 to 2025-09-30
* 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31
* 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31

The same logic should support monthly, quarterly, annual, or not applicable GST/QST filing frequencies.

### 7. Payroll and T5/RL3 Calendar Year Folders

Create or assist with flows to generate calendar-year folders for payroll and T5/RL3 documents, where applicable.

Payroll folders may include:

* Payroll Reports
* DAS / PD7A / TPZ Source Deductions
* Payroll Summaries
* T4 Slips and Summary
* RL-1 Slips and Summary
* CNESST / WSIB
* Taxable Benefits
* Car Allowance
* Employee Documents

### 8. Duplicate Prevention and Error Handling

The flows must include reasonable controls to prevent duplicate folder creation.

For example:

* If the client folder already exists, do not recreate it.
* If the fiscal year folder already exists, skip or notify the user.
* If a GST/QST period folder already exists, skip or notify the user.

We would also like a simple automation log or error notification system.

### 9. Permissions and Security Review

Review the proposed access model and recommend a secure but practical permissions structure for a small CPA firm.

We are not necessarily looking for complex folder-level permissions at the beginning, but we want to avoid mistakes that would be difficult to fix later.

### 10. Optional Metadata and Views

If appropriate, recommend and/or configure simple metadata and SharePoint views, such as:

* Client
* Fiscal Year
* Calendar Year
* Document Type
* Status
* Responsible Person

However, the solution should remain practical and easy for the team to use.

## Important Notes

We already have the accounting and professional filing logic. We are looking for technical implementation, automation, and SharePoint best practices.

The ideal solution should be:

* Easy to use by a small accounting team
* Scalable for many corporate clients
* Compatible with clients having different fiscal year-ends
* Compatible with monthly, quarterly, annual, or no GST/QST filing requirements
* Robust enough to avoid duplicate folders and automation errors
* Secure and suitable for confidential client information

## Required Skills

The freelancer should have strong experience with:

* Microsoft SharePoint Online
* Power Automate
* Microsoft 365
* SharePoint document libraries
* SharePoint lists
* Folder automation
* Conditional logic in Power Automate
* Error handling and logging
* Permission management in SharePoint

Experience working with accounting firms, legal firms, professional services firms, or document-heavy environments would be a strong asset.

## Deliverables

Expected deliverables include:

1. Reviewed and confirmed SharePoint implementation plan
2. SharePoint document library structure
3. Client Master List setup or refinement
4. Power Automate flow for new client folder creation
5. Power Automate flow for fiscal year folder creation
6. GST/QST period generation logic
7. Payroll and T5/RL3 calendar year folder logic, if applicable
8. Duplicate prevention logic
9. Basic error logging or notification
10. Short documentation explaining how to use and maintain the flows

## Preferred Approach

We would prefer to start with a short discovery/review session, followed by implementation in stages.

The first stage should be a working prototype using test clients only. Once validated, the automation can be applied to real clients.

## Questions for Applicants

Please answer the following when applying:

1. Have you implemented SharePoint folder automation using Power Automate before?
2. Can you create folders dynamically based on fiscal year-end dates and filing frequencies?
3. How would you prevent duplicate folder creation in Power Automate?
4. Do you recommend using folders only, metadata, document sets, or a hybrid approach for this type of project?
5. Have you worked with professional services firms or confidential client document structures before?
6. Are you able to provide a short handover document at the end of the project?

## Budget

Please provide an estimate based on the scope above. We are open to either a fixed-price project or an hourly arrangement, provided that the work is divided into clear milestones.

items.title: Part-Time Zoho One / Zoho CRM Implementation Freelancer — CRM to Inventory Roadmap
items.description:
Zoho One Implementation Contractor – Part-Time / Remote
Orange Cheese Company is a small U.S.-based international dairy trading and market-development company. We are implementing Zoho One as our U.S. business operating system and are looking for an experienced, hands-on Zoho contractor to help us set it up and launch it.
This is not a large ERP implementation and not a pure project-management role. We want someone who can personally configure Zoho, work directly with our management and users, and get a simple, practical system running quickly.
Initial project
We will start with one business unit, our Rest of Asia business, and build around real customers and active opportunities.
The first step is CRM:
Customer → Contact → Opportunity → Product/Application Need → Stage → Next Action
Once CRM is working well, we expect to extend the workflow into:
Product Development / NPD → Sourcing → Suppliers → Quotations → Purchasing → Supply Chain / Shipment → Financial Visibility
What we need from you
- Hands-on Zoho CRM / Zoho One implementation experience
- Personally configure modules, fields, layouts, views, workflows and permissions
- Import and organize existing data
- Build useful reports and dashboards
- Help us design simple workflows around how our business actually operates
- Test the system with real transactions and improve it based on user feedback
- Document the setup and train users
- Experience with Zoho Inventory, Books, Analytics, Projects or WorkDrive is a plus
- Trading, distribution, sourcing or supply-chain experience is a strong plus
How we will work
Our Rest of Asia business leader will be the primary business user. We have an on-site employee who can support data gathering and testing. The owners will work directly with the contractor on architecture and key decisions.
The work is fully remote. We expect approximately 10–20 hours per week initially, with an initial engagement of roughly 3 months. If the relationship works well, the engagement may continue as we expand Zoho.
We prefer standard Zoho functionality and simple configuration first. We do not want unnecessary customization or an enterprise-scale implementation methodology.
When applying, please answer these three questions:
1. Describe one Zoho implementation that you personally configured and launched. What did you actually build yourself?
2. Which Zoho applications are you comfortable configuring hands-on?
3. If you joined us, what would you try to accomplish during your first two weeks?
We expect to begin with a small paid working assignment before committing to the full implementation.

items.title: Reels Editor + Storyteller for Travel/Overlanding Brand
items.description:
We’re driving across Africa in a 20-year-old Toyota Land Cruiser, and we’re looking for someone who can turn the adventure into Reels people actually want to watch.

We’re looking for a creative short-form video editor/storyteller to help us grow Beyond Comfort on Instagram and TikTok.

This has the potential to become a long-term / full-time opportunity for the right person.

About Us

We’re Gigi and Paulina, a couple traveling across Africa by 4x4.

Our journey started in Georgia, where we bought an old Toyota Land Cruiser, fixed it up, and started driving across countries we'd never experienced before.

We’re not professional overlanders or filmmakers. We’re learning as we go, meeting people, trying new food, experiencing different cultures, getting ourselves into unexpected situations, and figuring things out along the way.

That’s what Beyond Comfort is about: stepping outside what’s familiar and seeing what happens.

We want our content to feel real, curious, funny, human, and occasionally ridiculous.

What We're Looking For

We need someone who can take raw footage and find the story or idea hiding inside it.

Our Reels aren't simply:
 Pretty landscape + trending song + text.

We want content with a reason to stop scrolling.

That could be:

- A funny or unexpected situation
- An interesting person we meet
- A cultural discovery
 - A ridiculous problem with our Land Cruiser
- A local food experience
- Something we completely misunderstood
- A surprising moment while traveling
- A beautiful place worth experiencing
- A story that makes people wonder, “What happened next?”

We want someone who understands that the hook comes first but the story has to deliver afterward.

 What You'll Do

You'll help us:

- Identify strong Reel ideas from raw footage
* Create compelling hooks
* Edit Instagram Reels and TikToks
* Structure videos for retention
* Cut dialogue naturally
* Select effective B-roll
* Add captions/subtitles
* Use music and sound effects appropriately
* Create engaging pacing
* Reframe footage for 9:16
* Apply basic color correction
* Suggest different hooks or approaches when useful

We're looking for someone with editorial judgment, not someone who simply follows a template.

We want you to be able to look at a folder of footage and say:

“There's a Reel in here.”

The Content

The places we visit are just as important as our personalities.

We want to showcase:
People • Food • Culture • Landscapes • Adventure • Overlanding • Unexpected moments

Our personalities and humor are part of the story, but we don't want to turn everything into influencer content.

The goal is to make someone stop scrolling because they're curious, stay because the story is good, and finish the Reel feeling like they experienced something with us.

Help Us Get Better Too

We're filming everything ourselves while traveling, so we're constantly learning.

Over time, we'd love for our editor to also give us practical feedback:

 “Next time, get this shot.”
 “Make sure you capture your reaction here.”
 “Get some clean ambient audio.”
 “Film this from another angle.”

We want to improve the footage we're sending you so the entire process becomes more efficient.

Better footage → better stories → better Reels.

Who We're Looking For

You'd be a great fit if you:

* Understand Instagram Reels and TikTok
* Have a strong instinct for hooks and retention
* Know how to tell a story in 20–60 seconds
* Have a good sense of humor and pacing
* Know how to make dialogue engaging
* Understand B-roll and vertical composition
* Have strong music/sound instincts
* Can work independently and make creative decisions
* Communicate clearly in English
* Are genuinely interested in travel, culture, adventure, or storytelling

Experience with travel, documentary, adventure, or personal-brand content is a plus, but great short-form storytelling matters more than the category you've worked in.

Not Our Style

We're probably not the right account for you if your editing is primarily:

* Generic trend-based content
* Constant transitions and effects
* Excessive zooms
* Meme edits without a story
* Generic travel montages

We're not trying to manufacture an influencer persona.

We're documenting a real adventure and making it entertaining.

Long-Term Potential

We'll start by testing the fit with a small project.

If things go well, we'd love for you to become the main short-form editor/creator for Beyond Comfort.

Over time, we'd like you to understand our personalities, humor, storytelling style, and what makes a Beyond Comfort Reel feel like a Beyond Comfort Reel.

As the channel grows, this could develop into consistent ongoing work and potentially a full-time position.

How to Apply

Please send us:

1. 3–5 Reels you've edited
Links to published videos are preferred. Please make clear which parts you personally edited.

2. Your portfolio
Any other relevant short-form work is welcome.

3. Tell us briefly: What makes someone stop scrolling?
We’re interested in how you think about hooks and retention.

4. What's your typical turnaround time for one Reel?

5. Have you worked with creators who film their own content?
If so, tell us briefly about the workflow.

Shortlisted Candidates: Mini Test

After reviewing applications, we'll shortlist our strongest candidates and invite them to complete a short editing test using some of our existing footage.

The test will be short and completely free, and we'll provide the footage and basic context.

We're not looking for a huge amount of work. We simply want to see what you naturally do with our footage — your hook, storytelling instincts, pacing, music, captions, and overall creative approach.

This will be an important part of our final selection.

We believe this is much more useful than choosing someone based purely on a portfolio, because we want to see how your editing style works with Beyond Comfort's actual footage and storytelling.

We're not looking for someone who can just make a video look good.

We're looking for someone who can watch a messy folder of footage from Africa and think:
“Wait. There's a Reel in here.”

If that's how your brain works, we'd love to see your work.

We can discuss pricing for the right candidate.

items.title: Inspirational Book on Failure, Faith, Spirituality & Personal Growth
items.description:
Inspirational Ghostwriter Needed for 30,000–35,000 Word Book on Failure, Faith, Spirituality & Personal Growth

I am looking for an experienced ghostwriter/co-writer to help develop an approximately 30,000–35,000-word inspirational nonfiction book aimed primarily at young adults/Gen Z.

The book will combine personal memoir, spirituality, lessons from failure, personal accountability, resilience, and inspirational historical examples. The central idea is that a serious mistake or failure does not necessarily define a person's life; what matters is how someone responds to it, learns from it, accepts responsibility, and uses it as a catalyst for growth.

 Core themes

The book will explore ideas such as:

- The role of spirituality and faith in the lives of Gen Z
- Faith in oneself and faith in God during periods of failure or uncertainty
- How failure can create determination, humility, maturity, and purpose
- Taking responsibility for mistakes instead of blaming circumstances or others
- The instinct people have to hide or rationalize mistakes—and the importance of confronting them
- Learning from failure rather than repeatedly making the same mistakes
- How success can create its own dangers if a person loses humility, values, or spiritual grounding
- The idea that a painful experience can ultimately become a turning point
- Second chances, forgiveness, accountability, and redemption
- Developing the ability to pause before making consequential decisions
- How spirituality, meditation, reflection, and self-awareness can help young people deal with pressure

A major part of the book will be based on a real personal experience involving one serious decision that had significant personal and professional consequences. The story should be written with honesty and accountability. The goal is not to excuse or minimize the mistake, but to explain what was learned from it and how it changed the author's approach to responsibility, faith, decision-making, and life.

More sensitive details of the personal story will be provided to the selected writer.

 Historical and inspirational examples

I would also like the book to incorporate carefully researched stories of well-known people who experienced rejection, failure, hardship, or major setbacks before accomplishing something meaningful.

Possible examples include:

Abraham Lincoln, Thomas Edison, Beethoven, Albert Einstein, Walt Disney, Winston Churchill, Michael Jordan, Colonel Sanders, the Wright Brothers, Tony Robbins, Babe Ruth, and others.

There may also be discussion of religious, philosophical, and historical figures—including examples from Hindu philosophy and other spiritual traditions—where appropriate.

All historical anecdotes and quotations must be fact-checked. I do not want commonly repeated internet stories included simply because they sound inspirational.

 Tone

The writing should be:

- Inspirational without sounding cliché
- Spiritual without becoming overly preachy
- Personal and emotionally engaging
- Reflective and mature
- Accessible to readers in their late teens and twenties
- Professionally written enough that physicians, educators, mentors, and professional leaders could comfortably read it
- Honest about failure without becoming self-pitying
- Focused on accountability rather than justification
- Hopeful without exaggerating the author's transformation

Think of the project as a combination of memoir + personal development + spirituality + practical lessons for young adults.

 Possible book concept/title

One working concept is:

I Thought I Had Failed 
The Exam I Passed and the Test I Almost Lost

Other possible themes/titles include:

The Price of One Night 
How a Single Decision Nearly Cost Me Everything, and What It Taught Me

The Cost of a Moment 
What One Mistake Taught Me About Fear, Faith, and Becoming Better

The Pause That Saves a Life 
Spiritual Tools for Young People Under Pressure

The final title and chapter structure can be developed collaboratively with the writer.

 Expected length and structure

Target length: 30,000–35,000 words, approximately 100–130 paperback pages depending on formatting.

I am envisioning approximately 10–12 chapters, potentially including:

1. The personal turning point
2. Why intelligent people still make poor decisions
3. Failure versus being a failure
4. Accountability
5. Faith when life does not go according to plan
6. What history teaches us about failure
7. Spirituality in a Gen Z world
8. Learning to pause under pressure
9. Success, ego, and staying grounded
10. Forgiveness and second chances
11. Turning regret into service
12. Moving forward with purpose

This is only a preliminary framework. I am looking for a writer who can help substantially improve the structure.

 Deliverables

The selected writer will:

- Review my notes, stories, and background material
- Conduct several interviews with me as needed
- Develop a detailed chapter outline
- Help determine the strongest narrative structure
- Research and fact-check historical examples
- Write approximately 30,000–35,000 words
- Incorporate personal stories naturally rather than making the book read like a collection of motivational quotes
- Complete revisions based on feedback
- Deliver an edited final manuscript suitable for digital publication and later paperback formatting

The book does not need to be physically published immediately. The initial goal is a polished manuscript that can be distributed/read digitally, with the possibility of formal publication later.

 Timeline

Ideally, I would like the manuscript completed within approximately 2–3 weeks.

Because this is a relatively fast turnaround, please apply only if you have the availability to work intensively on the project during that period.

 Ideal candidate

I am especially interested in writers with experience in one or more of the following:

- Memoir/autobiography
- Inspirational nonfiction
- Personal development
- Spirituality
- Psychology or behavioral science
- Medical/professional memoir
- Writing for Gen Z/young adults
- Ghostwriting books for professionals

You should be comfortable writing about mistakes, personal accountability, spirituality, professional pressure, and redemption in a nuanced way.

Strong interviewing skills are also important. I want the book to sound like my voice and my story, rather than a generic motivational book.

 Confidentiality

Some parts of the story are personal and professionally sensitive. The selected writer must be comfortable maintaining strict confidentiality and, if requested, signing an NDA.

 When applying

Please include:

1. A brief description of your ghostwriting/book-writing experience.
2. Links or samples of relevant nonfiction, memoir, inspirational, or spirituality writing.
3. Whether you can complete a 30,000–35,000-word manuscript within approximately 2–3 weeks.
4. Your proposed fixed-price budget.
5. How many rounds of revision your proposal includes.
6. How you normally conduct author interviews.
7. A short explanation of how you would keep a book about failure and spirituality from sounding cliché or preachy.

Please begin your proposal with the words “Failure Is Not Final” so I know you have read the entire description.

- The role of spirituality and faith in the lives of Gen Z
- Faith in oneself and faith in God during periods of failure or uncertainty
- How failure can create determination, humility, maturity, and purpose
- Taking responsibility for mistakes instead of blaming circumstances or others
- The instinct people have to hide or rationalize mistakes—and the importance of confronting them
- Learning from failure rather than repeatedly making the same mistakes
- How success can create its own dangers if a person loses humility, values, or spiritual grounding
- The idea that a painful experience can ultimately become a turning point
- Second chances, forgiveness, accountability, and redemption
- Developing the ability to pause before making consequential decisions
- How spirituality, meditation, reflection, and self-awareness can help young people deal with pressure

A major part of the book will be based on a real personal experience involving one serious decision that had significant personal and professional consequences. The story should be written with honesty and accountability. The goal is not to excuse or minimize the mistake, but to explain what was learned from it and how it changed the author's approach to responsibility, faith, decision-making, and life.

More sensitive details of the personal story will be provided to the selected writer.

 Historical and inspirational examples

I would also like the book to incorporate carefully researched stories of well-known people who experienced rejection, failure, hardship, or major setbacks before accomplishing something meaningful.

Possible examples include:

Abraham Lincoln, Thomas Edison, Beethoven, Albert Einstein, Walt Disney, Winston Churchill, Michael Jordan, Colonel Sanders, the Wright Brothers, Tony Robbins, Babe Ruth, and others.

There may also be discussion of religious, philosophical, and historical figures—including examples from Hindu philosophy and other spiritual traditions—where appropriate.

All historical anecdotes and quotations must be fact-checked. I do not want commonly repeated internet stories included simply because they sound inspirational.

 Tone

The writing should be:

- Inspirational without sounding cliché
- Spiritual without becoming overly preachy
- Personal and emotionally engaging
- Reflective and mature
- Accessible to readers in their late teens and twenties
- Professionally written enough that physicians, educators, mentors, and professional leaders could comfortably read it
- Honest about failure without becoming self-pitying
- Focused on accountability rather than justification
- Hopeful without exaggerating the author's transformation

Think of the project as a combination of memoir + personal development + spirituality + practical lessons for young adults.

 Possible book concept/title

One working concept is:

I Thought I Had Failed 
The Exam I Passed and the Test I Almost Lost

Other possible themes/titles include:

The Price of One Night 
How a Single Decision Nearly Cost Me Everything, and What It Taught Me

The Cost of a Moment 
What One Mistake Taught Me About Fear, Faith, and Becoming Better

The Pause That Saves a Life 
Spiritual Tools for Young People Under Pressure

The final title and chapter structure can be developed collaboratively with the writer.

 Expected length and structure

Target length: 30,000–35,000 words, approximately 100–130 paperback pages depending on formatting.

I am envisioning approximately 10–12 chapters, potentially including:

1. The personal turning point
2. Why intelligent people still make poor decisions
3. Failure versus being a failure
4. Accountability
5. Faith when life does not go according to plan
6. What history teaches us about failure
7. Spirituality in a Gen Z world
8. Learning to pause under pressure
9. Success, ego, and staying grounded
10. Forgiveness and second chances
11. Turning regret into service
12. Moving forward with purpose

This is only a preliminary framework. I am looking for a writer who can help substantially improve the structure.

 Deliverables

The selected writer will:

- Review my notes, stories, and background material
- Conduct several interviews with me as needed
- Develop a detailed chapter outline
- Help determine the strongest narrative structure
- Research and fact-check historical examples
- Write approximately 30,000–35,000 words
- Incorporate personal stories naturally rather than making the book read like a collection of motivational quotes
- Complete revisions based on feedback
- Deliver an edited final manuscript suitable for digital publication and later paperback formatting

The book does not need to be physically published immediately. The initial goal is a polished manuscript that can be distributed/read digitally, with the possibility of formal publication later.

 Timeline

Ideally, I would like the manuscript completed within approximately 2–3 weeks.

Because this is a relatively fast turnaround, please apply only if you have the availability to work intensively on the project during that period.

 Ideal candidate

I am especially interested in writers with experience in one or more of the following:

- Memoir/autobiography
- Inspirational nonfiction
- Personal development
- Spirituality
- Psychology or behavioral science
- Medical/professional memoir
- Writing for Gen Z/young adults
- Ghostwriting books for professionals

You should be comfortable writing about mistakes, personal accountability, spirituality, professional pressure, and redemption in a nuanced way.

Strong interviewing skills are also important. I want the book to sound like my voice and my story, rather than a generic motivational book.

 Confidentiality

Some parts of the story are personal and professionally sensitive. The selected writer must be comfortable maintaining strict confidentiality and, if requested, signing an NDA.

 When applying

Please include:

1. A brief description of your ghostwriting/book-writing experience.
2. Links or samples of relevant nonfiction, memoir, inspirational, or spirituality writing.
3. Whether you can complete a 30,000–35,000-word manuscript within approximately 2–3 weeks.
4. Your proposed fixed-price budget.
5. How many rounds of revision your proposal includes.
6. How you normally conduct author interviews.
7. A short explanation of how you would keep a book about failure and spirituality from sounding cliché or preachy.

Please begin your proposal with the words “Failure Is Not Final” so I know you have read the entire description.

items.title: Shopify technical SEO + Liquid + website speed + Meta & Google tracking
items.description:
Hi,
I’m looking for an experienced Shopify developer who understands Shopify Liquid, technical SEO, website speed optimisation, Meta Pixel/CAPI and Google tracking.
My Shopify website is already live and I already have an SEO audit. I do NOT need another audit, SEO report, monthly SEO package or ongoing management.
I need someone to implement the fixes directly in my Shopify store, test everything properly, and complete this as a one-time project.
1. H1 / H2 HEADING STRUCTURE
- Check the entire website for incorrect H1/H2 structure.
- Some pages currently have multiple H1 headings.
- Some important collection/product pages currently have no proper H1.
- Fix the homepage, collection pages, product pages and other important pages.
- Make sure each important page has one appropriate primary H1 and a logical H2/H3 structure.
- Fix the Shopify Liquid/theme code where necessary rather than simply changing the visual appearance of headings.
- Make sure these changes do not damage the existing website design.
2. TECHNICAL & ON-PAGE SEO
- Review and optimise SEO page titles.
- Fix missing or duplicate meta descriptions.
- Review important product and collection pages for SEO.
- Check URLs and existing redirects for problems.
- Check canonical tags.
- Check internal linking.
- Check XML sitemap.
- Check crawlability and indexing.
- Check schema/structured data and fix relevant errors or duplication.
- Check for broken links and other important technical SEO problems.
- Check Google Search Console, sitemap submission, indexing and relevant errors.
I want the problems fixed, not simply listed in another report.
3. IMAGE SEO / ALT TEXT
- Review images across the homepage, collection pages, product pages and other important website pages.
- Add missing ALT text where appropriate.
- Improve poor or meaningless ALT text.
- Write descriptive, relevant and SEO-appropriate ALT text.
- Use keywords naturally where relevant — no keyword stuffing.
- Do not unnecessarily replace ALT text that is already good.
- Handle decorative images appropriately.
4. WEBSITE SPEED & PERFORMANCE
- Test website performance on mobile and desktop before optimisation.
- Improve Google PageSpeed / Core Web Vitals, with particular attention to mobile.
- Investigate unnecessary or slow theme scripts/code.
- Check whether Shopify apps or leftover app code are slowing down the website.
- Check oversized/unoptimised images and image loading.
- Optimise lazy loading where appropriate.
- Improve JavaScript/CSS performance where reasonably possible.
- Improve LCP, INP and CLS where possible.
- Do not remove important functionality or negatively change the website design simply to achieve a higher PageSpeed score.
- Test again after optimisation and provide before-and-after performance results.
5. META PIXEL + CONVERSIONS API
- Check that the correct Meta Pixel is connected to Shopify.
- Check whether there are duplicate or old Meta Pixels.
- Test important ecommerce events, including:
 - ViewContent
 - AddToCart
 - InitiateCheckout
 - Purchase
- Check Meta Conversions API (CAPI).
- Make sure browser Pixel and CAPI events are working correctly together.
- Check for duplicate event reporting/deduplication problems.
- Check whether old apps, theme code or other integrations are creating duplicate Meta events.
6. GOOGLE ANALYTICS + GOOGLE ADS TRACKING
- Check Google Analytics 4 (GA4) installation.
- Make sure Shopify ecommerce events are being recorded correctly.
- Test purchase/conversion tracking.
- Check Google Ads conversion tracking.
- Make sure purchases/conversions are not being counted twice.
- Check for duplicate Google tags.
- Check whether Google Tag Manager, old theme code or apps are causing duplicate tracking.
- Check the Shopify Google & YouTube integration.
- Check relevant Google Merchant Center connection/setup.
7. GOOGLE SEARCH CONSOLE
- Check that the correct website/domain is connected.
- Check sitemap submission.
- Check indexing status.
- Investigate relevant indexing/crawling errors.
- Check important pages are accessible to Google.
- Fix technical issues within Shopify where required.
8. SAFETY — VERY IMPORTANT
My website is already live.
Before changing any theme/Liquid code, please duplicate/back up my current live Shopify theme.
Please:
- Do not make unnecessary design changes.
- Do not install unnecessary Shopify apps.
- Do not remove functionality without discussing it with me first.
- Do not change important URLs without checking redirects.
- Test important website functions after completing the work.
9. FINAL TESTING & HANDOVER
When the project is finished, I would like:
- Confirmation that the H1/H2 problems have been fixed.
- Confirmation that technical SEO issues included in the agreed scope have been fixed.
- Confirmation that ALT text has been reviewed/fixed.
- Before/after website speed results.
- Confirmation that Meta Pixel and CAPI are working correctly.
- Confirmation that GA4 and Google Ads ecommerce/conversion tracking are working correctly.
- Confirmation that duplicate tracking has been checked.
- Confirmation that Google Search Console/indexing has been checked.
- A short summary of exactly what you changed.
I do not need a large SEO report. I need the actual work completed and tested.
PROJECT TERMS
This is a ONE-TIME FIXED-PRICE PROJECT ONLY.
I am NOT looking for:
- Monthly SEO management
- An ongoing retainer
- Monthly backlink packages
- Another automated SEO audit
- Someone who only provides recommendations without implementing them
I would ideally like the project completed within approximately 2–4 days.
Before I hire you, please answer:
1. What is your fixed price for the complete scope above?
2. Approximately how many hours do you expect the work to take?
3. How quickly can you complete it?
4. Do you personally work with Shopify Liquid/theme code?
5. Do you have experience fixing Shopify H1/H2 and technical SEO issues?
6. Do you have experience with Meta Pixel + Conversions API on Shopify?
7. Do you have experience with GA4 + Google Ads conversion tracking on Shopify?
8. Do you have experience with Shopify speed/Core Web Vitals optimisation?
9. Will you implement all agreed fixes yourself, rather than simply provide another audit?
10. Can you provide examples of similar Shopify work you have completed?
Please confirm exactly what is included in your fixed price before we start.

items.title: Wikidata & Google Knowledge Panel Specialist for a Fintech Founder
items.description:
The goal of this engagement is a Google Knowledge Panel for the client, a fintech founder and Forbes Business Council member. You will build the entity foundation on Wikidata and advise on the identity footprint that feeds the panel.

A lot of groundwork is already done:
- The client's primary bio page is live with JSON-LD Person schema deployed and validating clean
- A complete digital-footprint dossier is compiled: 23 verified links across company sites, founder profiles, social accounts, corporate records, and media mentions
- Corporate records are gathered, including state entity filings and a July 2026 SEC Form D
- The Crunchbase founder profile is updated with current photo, titles, and bio
- A Ballotpedia update is submitted and under staff review; an IMDb bio update is filed and processing
- Investor deck and verified company documentation are on hand

Deliverables:
1. A new, policy-compliant Wikidata item (person) with accurate statements, qualifiers, and references to reliable sources for every claim
2. Proper linking: sitelinks where they exist, identifiers (VIAF/ISNI etc.) where obtainable, and correct instance-of / occupation / employer statements
3. A short written assessment of notability standing under Wikidata's notability policy, and an honest read on Wikipedia article viability (no promises, no guarantees, I want the truth)
4. A Knowledge Panel readiness review: what is already in place, what is missing, and a prioritized punch list of the 3 to 5 highest-value sources or citations to obtain next

Requirements:
- Demonstrable history of Wikidata contributions (link your user page / edit history)
- Working knowledge of Wikidata notability policy and referencing standards
- You must comply with all paid-contribution disclosure requirements on any Wikimedia project you touch
- Clear written English; you will document every statement you add and why

Nice to have:
- Experience with Wikipedia article creation through AfC
- Familiarity with Google Knowledge Panels / entity SEO and sameAs strategy
- Experience sourcing founder/executive profiles

How to apply:
1. Link 2-3 Wikidata items or Wikipedia articles you have created or substantially improved
2. In 3-4 sentences, describe how you would approach sourcing for a living businessperson whose coverage is currently thin on independent press


Note: this posting intentionally contains no links or names. The full dossier and all assets are shared after hire.

items.title: Google Ads + Meta Ads Manager for Real Estate Wholesaler (US Only)
items.description:
Title: US-Based Google Ads + Meta Ads Manager for Real Estate Wholesaler (Motivated Seller Leads)

We're a multi-state real estate wholesaling company (Florida, Indiana, Ohio, Michigan) buying houses directly from homeowners. We're looking for one US-based individual to take over and manage our Google Ads and Meta Ads long term. No agencies and no outsourced work, please.

Ad spend: $15K+/month across both platforms, with room to scale for the right results.

What you'll do:
- Audit our existing Google Ads and Meta accounts and rebuild where needed
- Manage Google Search campaigns targeting motivated sellers ("sell my house fast," "cash home buyers," etc.)
- Manage Meta lead gen campaigns within the Housing Special Ad Category
- Set up and maintain conversion tracking, including offline conversions from GoHighLevel, so campaigns optimize toward qualified leads and signed contracts
- Maintain negative keyword lists and keep lead quality high
- Keep both accounts fully policy compliant
- Send a weekly report: spend, leads, cost per lead, qualified leads, contracts

Requirements:
- Based in the US, available for a weekly call during US business hours
- Proven experience running motivated seller campaigns for wholesalers, cash buyers, or investors (this is required, general real estate agent experience doesn't count)
- Experience with offline conversion tracking and GoHighLevel or a similar CRM
- You do the work yourself

To apply, start your proposal with the word "seller" and include:
1. Screenshots from a motivated seller account you've managed, showing spend, cost per lead, and time period
2. The average cost per lead and cost per contract you'd expect at our budget
3. What you'd check first in our accounts during week one

We'll start with a paid audit of our current accounts. If it's a fit, we move to a monthly retainer.

items.title: Allplan Bridge Specialist: 3D Rebar Model, Shop Drawings and BBS
items.description:
ABOUT US
Engineering Support Group (ESG) is an engineering consultancy delivering bridge, civil and structural engineering across the Gulf. We are preparing the reinforcement shop drawings for a new bridge and need an Allplan Bridge specialist to join our team for this package.

THE PROJECT
- Structure: [Box Girder]. Drawings would be shared later.
- Elements in scope: [deck slab, girders, diaphragms, pier caps, piers, abutments, pile caps, approach slabs]
- Design code: [AASHTO LRFD / Eurocode 2 / BS]; bar schedules to [BS 8666:2020]
- We provide: approved design drawings (PDF and DWG), our title block and drawing standards
- Start: [date], subject to final award

SCOPE OF WORK
1. Build or update the parametric Allplan Bridge model (alignment, cross-sections, superstructure, substructure) from the approved design drawings.
2. Model all reinforcement in 3D, including variable cross-sections, skew and curvature where they apply.
3. Coordinate reinforcement with tendons, anchorages, bearings, drainage and other embedded items, and resolve clashes.
4. Produce reinforcement shop drawings (plans, sections, details) on our title block.
5. Extract bar bending schedules from the model to [BS 8666:2020].
6. Revise drawings and schedules after the consultant's review comments, [2] review cycles included.

DELIVERABLES
- Native Allplan files that open in Allplan 2024
- Shop drawings in PDF and DWG
- Bar bending schedules in Excel and PDF
- IFC export of the reinforced model
- A list of any discrepancies found in the design drawings

REQUIREMENTS
- Your own licensed Allplan with the Bridge and reinforcement modules
- At least [2] bridges reinforced in Allplan, with samples you can show (building-only rebar experience is not enough)
- Experience with bridge elements of variable geometry
- Good written English

NICE TO HAVE
- Experience with GCC shop drawing submissions and consultant review cycles
- Allplan Bridge scripting (TCL or Python)

HOW WE WILL WORK
- Milestone 1 is a paid pilot: one [pier / span] fully reinforced, drawn and scheduled. The rest of the package is awarded on the quality of the pilot.
- Project drawings are shared after shortlisting and a signed NDA.
- Weekly progress calls on Teams or Zoom with a screen-share of the live model.

TO APPLY
Answer the screening questions and attach bridge reinforcement drawings or model screenshots you produced in Allplan. Proposals without bridge samples will not be considered.

items.title: High-End Web Designer & Landing Page Specialist
items.description:
We’re seeking a skilled web designer to create polished, conversion-focused landing pages for our business. You’ll work closely with our team to turn ideas into visually strong, user-friendly pages that support our brand and drive results. The ideal freelancer has experience building high-quality websites and landing pages, can translate concepts into effective layouts, and is comfortable collaborating with stakeholders to refine designs. This is a part-time opportunity for someone who can deliver clean, professional work and help improve our online presence.


We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Web Designer & Website Specialist with proven experience in WordPress and Bluehost to help us create, maintain, and optimize high-end, elegant, and professional websites and landing pages.

The ideal candidate must be able to build landing pages from scratch, handling both the visual design and the page content and structure, while ensuring a seamless user experience and a polished, premium look.

The role also includes ongoing website maintenance and optimization, basic SEO implementation, and working with Google Analytics to monitor website performance and identify opportunities for improvement.

Experience with Kajabi is a plus.

Responsibilities:

-Design and build high-quality, visually appealing landing pages from scratch.
-Handle the entire landing page creation process, including layout, design, content structure, and page elements.
- Create elegant, modern, and professional designs aligned with our brand identity.
- Manage, maintain, and update websites using WordPress and Bluehost.
- Maintain and optimize existing website pages to improve functionality, performance, and user experience.
- Implement basic on-page SEO best practices, including page structure, headings, metadata, and content optimization.
- Work with Google Analytics to monitor website traffic, user behavior, and overall website performance.
- Identify opportunities to improve website performance, user experience, SEO, and conversions.
-Optimize pages for desktop and mobile devices.
- Improve website layouts, typography, visual hierarchy, and overall user experience.
- Implement feedback and make revisions efficiently.
- Ensure that all pages are functional, visually consistent, optimized, and professionally presented.
- Perform ongoing website maintenance and troubleshooting as needed.

Requirements:

- Proven experience with WordPress and Bluehost is mandatory.
- Kajabi is a plus 
- Strong portfolio showcasing high-end, elegant, and professional website designs.
-Demonstrated ability to create complete landing pages from scratch, including design and content organization.
-Experience maintaining and optimizing existing websites.
-Good understanding of SEO and on-page SEO best practices.
-Experience with Google Analytics and understanding of basic website performance metrics.
-Excellent understanding of layout, typography, visual hierarchy, and user experience.
-Ability to work independently, meet deadlines, and deliver high-quality results efficiently.
-Strong communication skills and attention to detail.
-Ability to troubleshoot website issues and implement improvements proactively.

Hourly Rate:

$10–$13 per hour, depending on experience and skills.

How to Apply

Please include the following in your proposal:

Your portfolio with examples of websites and landing pages you have designed from scratch.
A brief description of your experience with WordPress and Bluehost.
Examples of landing pages where you handled both the design and content structure.
Examples of website maintenance and optimization work you have completed.
A brief description of your SEO experience and the types of SEO tasks you have handled.
Your experience with Google Analytics, including what you typically use it for.
Your experience with Kajabi, if applicable.
Your availability and estimated weekly working hours.

items.title: High-Ticket Appointment Setter – E-commerce Education Sales
items.description:
About the role
Launch E runs the full sales engine for e-commerce education brands (Amazon FBA, Shopify, eBay, Dropshipping). As our Appointment Setter, you are the first voice our leads hear. You reach people who already bought a course, qualify them and fill our closer's calendar with high-intent calls for $3K–$10K programs.
We're looking for someone with at least 6 months of experience in appointment setting, BDR/SDR, outbound or inside sales, who understands how a setter and a closer work together. You speak English at a native or C2 level, clear and easy to follow on the phone. Bonus if you have experience in high-ticket, coaching, online education or e-commerce sales, or if you're based in the US or Canada.

Responsibilities
- Contact assigned leads: recent course buyers and abandoned checkouts
- Follow our script with the right tone and energy
- Qualify each prospect's motivation, capital and fit
- Handle first objections and book calls with our closer
- Follow up by phone, SMS, DMs and LinkedIn
- Log every interaction in the CRM
- Join a 15-minute daily call review and share script feedback

Tools you'll use
Phone — to call and qualify leads
SMS and DMs — to follow up and confirm appointments
LinkedIn — to reach and re-engage prospects
CRM — to track leads, calls and booked appointments
Slack — to get live support from the team during deals

What we offer
Pay: base + performance commission; competitive, shared during the process
Schedule & modality: Remote · 30 hours/week within 9am–5pm EST
Contract type: Independent contractor
Leads provided: no list building
Commissions paid weekly, every Friday
Ready-to-use script and daily coaching
Onboarding: product briefing and live roleplay with our sales director

HVAC and mechanical service company looking for a reliable, confident, highly organized Customer Service Representative who can help us turn new inquiries into appointments and long-term customer relationships.

* Answer and return customer calls, texts, emails, and website leads

You will not diagnose HVAC problems. Technical diagnosis and recommendations are handled by our qualified field professionals.

Experience with platforms such as GoHighLevel,m, Jobber, HubSpot, Google Workspace, or similar CRM/field-service systems is a plus.

How Success Will Be Measured
We will focus on response time, appointment booking rate, follow-up completion, CRM accuracy, membership conversions, customer satisfaction, reviews, referrals, and recovered opportunities, not simply the number of calls answered.

items.title: 15 real Android testers for a 14-day Google Play closed test (kids' learning app)
items.description:
I'm the developer of HK Little Stars, an Android learning app for children in Uganda (nursery to Primary 7). The app has finished its closed-testing build. I now need Google Play's requirement met: at least 12 testers opted in continuously for 14 consecutive days, after which I apply for production access.

I'm hiring one freelancer who can supply and manage 15 testers (12 required + 3 buffer for drop-outs).

What each tester must do
- Use a real Android phone, Android 8 or newer. No emulators, no cloned or shared Google accounts, one tester per account.
- Give me their Gmail address before we start. I add testers by email list, not a public link.
- Tell me their country so I can enable it on the test track.
- Install from the Play closed-testing link and stay opted in and installed for the full 14 days, then until Google approves. Opting out early resets that tester's 14 days.
- Open and use the app at least 3 times a week. The app needs no sign-in: enter a name, pick a class, do lessons and quizzes.
- Day 1: finish one lesson in any class. Day 4: complete a quiz. Day 8: install the updated build when Play offers it and repeat one lesson.
- Fill in a short Google Form (5 questions) on day 4 and day 12: what worked, what confused them, phone model, Android version.

What you deliver
- The list of 15 Gmail addresses and countries within 24 hours of hire.
- The opt-in count in my Play Console staying at 12 or more every day for 14 days. I check the Testers tab daily and the track's device and country statistics.
- Both feedback rounds completed by every tester.
- A short summary at the end: devices used, bugs seen, which screens testers spent time on.

Payment
- Milestone 1, $10: released when 15 opt-ins show in Play Console.
- Milestone 2, $25: released on day 14 if the count never dropped below 12 and both feedback forms are in from every tester.
- Bonus $10 when Google grants production access.

Rules
- I'm paying for testers' time and written feedback. Nobody is paid for an install, a rating or a review, and I don't want any ratings or reviews.
- If a tester drops out, replace them the same day and tell me. A replacement starts their own 14 days, which is why we start with 15.
- Testers in Uganda or East Africa are preferred. Any country is fine if you tell me in advance.

Please answer the screening questions. Proposals that just say "I will provide 12 testers" won't be considered.

Screening questions:
1. Where are your testers based (countries), and are they people you know or a pool you share with other buyers?
2. How do you make sure testers actually open the app during the 14 days, not just opt in?
3. What do you do when a tester opts out on day 9?
4. Have you had a client's production-access application rejected for "testers were not engaged"? What changed afterwards?
5. Can you start within 48 hours and send the Gmail list within 24 hours of hire?

Skills: Android, Google Play Console, Mobile App Testing, Beta Testing, QA Testing

items.title: Full-Stack Developer (Node/React + DevOps): Build & Deploy Web and Mobile Apps
items.description:
About Us
We're a growing team at coolmarketing.com building web applications, internal tools, and client-facing products. We move quickly and work across a range of project types, so we need a versatile developer who can own a feature from architecture through deployment.

The Role
We're looking for a long-term offshore full-stack developer to help design, build, and ship applications. Our current stack is primarily Node.js, but we pick tools based on what each project needs, so you should be comfortable picking up new languages and frameworks quickly. Some projects are web-based, others are mobile.

What You'll Do

Build and maintain front-end and back-end features for web and mobile applications
Design application architecture, including databases, APIs, auth, and service structure
Set up and manage deployment pipelines and hosting on platforms like AWS, Vercel, Railway, or similar
Configure CI/CD, environment management, and monitoring
Integrate third-party APIs and services
Write clean, documented code that others on the team can pick up
Communicate progress, blockers, and technical tradeoffs clearly

Required Skills

Strong experience with Node.js and modern JavaScript/TypeScript
Solid front-end skills with React or a similar framework
Hands-on experience deploying production apps to AWS, Vercel, Railway, or equivalent platforms
Experience designing system architecture from scratch, not just working inside existing codebases
Comfort with SQL and NoSQL databases
Git and CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions or similar)
Ability to work across languages and stacks as projects require
Good written English and reliable communication

Nice to Have

React Native and Expo experience
Python, Go, or other backend languages
Docker and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CDK, etc.)
Experience building with data privacy or compliance requirements (for example, HIPAA)
Experience with SMS, email, or messaging integrations

What We Offer

Long-term, ongoing work with a variety of projects
Room to influence architecture and tooling decisions
Flexible hours, with some overlap with US Pacific time for meetings
Starting pay will be $3/ Per Hour, based on performance this is subject to change. 

How to Apply
Please include:

Two or three projects you've built and deployed, with links or screenshots, and your specific role in each
A short description of a deployment pipeline you set up: what platform, what tools, and why you chose them
Your experience with React Native / Expo, if any
Your hourly rate and weekly availability

Start your proposal with the word "Pipeline" so we know you read the full post. Proposals without it won't be reviewed.

items.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer – Low-Volume Manufacturing & Product Redesign
items.description:
**Project Type:** Freelance / Contract 
**Experience:** Senior-level mechanical engineering, DFM and manufacturing 
**Industry:** Consumer Electronics / Wearable Devices

## Project Overview

I have a working electronic wearable with existing STEP files, but the current enclosure design is prohibitively expensive to manufacture. I've received quotes exceeding $20,000 for production tooling, while alternative manufacturing methods have resulted in unacceptably high per-part costs.

I'm looking for an experienced engineer who can **take ownership of solving this manufacturing problem**, not simply produce another CAD design.

The goal is to develop a practical, affordable manufacturing strategy for an initial production run of 50–500 units, with the potential to scale to 1,000+ units.

Importantly, this product is still evolving. I anticipate additional versions and need a manufacturing process that accommodates design improvements without repeatedly investing in expensive tooling.

## Scope of Work

**Phase 1: Manufacturing Strategy and Feasibility**

- Review the existing STEP files and identify the design features driving manufacturing costs.
- Evaluate practical manufacturing alternatives, including low-volume injection molding, aluminum bridge tooling, modular tooling, vacuum casting and CNC machining.
- Identify opportunities to simplify the enclosure and reduce the number of custom components.
- Work with manufacturers and toolmakers to obtain realistic preliminary pricing.
- Develop a manufacturing roadmap covering 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1,000 units.
- Explain how future design revisions can be accommodated affordably.

**Phase 2: Enclosure Redesign and Production**

Following approval of the manufacturing roadmap:

- Redesign the enclosure around the selected manufacturing process.
- Preserve the external appearance and general dimensions where practical.
- Simplify internal geometry, assembly, button mechanisms and water sealing.
- Prepare manufacturing-ready CAD and coordinate with the selected manufacturer.
- Support prototype validation and the initial production run.

## Required Experience

I'm specifically looking for someone with hands-on experience taking physical consumer products from prototype to production.

Experience with DFM, low-volume manufacturing, injection molding, tooling cost reduction and supplier sourcing is essential. Experience with small electronic enclosures, waterproofing and wearable devices is highly desirable.

**This is not a CAD-only assignment.** I need someone who understands manufacturing economics, can propose affordable solutions and has experience working directly with manufacturers.

## Initial Deliverable

The first engagement will be a paid manufacturing-feasibility phase resulting in a clear, actionable plan that identifies:

- A recommended manufacturing process and enclosure architecture.
- Estimated tooling and per-unit costs at different production volumes.
- Specific design changes needed to achieve those costs.
- A strategy for affordable future product revisions.
- A practical path from the current prototype through initial production and eventual higher-volume manufacturing.

Please include examples of products you have personally helped bring into production, your experience reducing manufacturing costs, and how you would approach this project.

**I'm willing to pay for the engineering expertise required to solve this problem, but I need a viable manufacturing plan before investing in another full CAD redesign.**
